brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Hex bases piece:0,0,0 (full), piece:0,0,1 (full), piece:0,0,2 (full) stacked on one column, with snap connectors between them; check_build meshClash 'clear'.

Bottom storey (level 0) has notch:0#0,1#notch1, a 'Notch drawer frame (female-male hand)' at cell (0,1,0) between the full base (0,0,0) and half-w base (1,0,0), with a joint bolt on (1,0,0). I could not get the separate 'drawer' family to offer a placement (addDrawer needs a key the configurator never offered; the half-base cut face gave no drawer offers), so I am not certain the notch frame is a working drawer. Only one drawer position is built.

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,2~hex-bin-full (open full-depth tray) sitting in the top-storey base piece:0,0,2 (level 2).

finish.summary: Built a three-storey column: full hex bases at levels 0, 1 and 2, with snaps between them. The top storey holds an open full-depth bin. The bottom storey has one notch drawer frame at (0,1,0) beside a half base at (1,0,0), locked with a joint bolt. check_build reports meshClash clear and no rule errors. The drawer part is the weak point: the standalone drawer family never offered a placement, so the bottom storey may not be fully drawer-equipped. Only the single notch position is built.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
